genetic variation in SLC5A2 and GIPR is associated with increased GIP levels, whereas genetic variation in ABO is associated with increased GLP-1 levels.

we identified six novel genetic loci associated with circulating levels of incretin hormones in or near the GIPR, SLC5A2, ABO, F13A, HOXD1 and GLP2R genes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic determinants of the incretin hormones GIP and GLPL-1 and their effect on the risk of type 2 diabetes and related phenotypes.

the genetics of incretin hormones, which play an important role in the regulation of blood glucose concentrations.

the study provides candidate genes and some insight into the mechanism by which secretion and degradation of incretin hormones is regulated, but that the results do not provide evidence for a major role for these genetic variants for the regulation of incretin hormone secretion and glucose homeostasis in vivo.

this paper provides evidence for genetic determinants of circulating GLP-1 and GIP concentrations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we identified genetic variants that affect incretin concentrations in humans.
the genetic determinants of incretin concentrations are largely different from those of glucose, insulin, and glucagon, and are mainly located in genes involved in incretin metabolism.
we have found genetic variants associated with incretin hormone concentrations and that these variants may affect hormone secretion and breakdown.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have identified several genes involved in incretin secretion and metabolism that could be potential targets for new incretin therapies.
genetic variation at several genes is associated with plasma concentrations of incretin hormones.

the incretin hormones GIP and GLPs-1 are regulated in a complex fashion by multiple genetic factors and that these genetic determinants may have implications for the development of new treatment strategies for type-2 diabetes.
